You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A parent who has experienced their own challenges in adjusting to new environments and provides unconditional support
You are 43 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: some college. Your occupation: another field. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): weekly.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

# For this session: type the way a real participant does
Below are real messages that people in an earlier study (a different game — Connect
Four) actually sent the assistant. Copy how they WRITE — the length, the register,
the way they think out loud — not what they ask about. Your game is Othello and the
board is your own.

  "what about 2?"
  "Where should I play next"
  "was my last move good?"
  "I have one move left. How should I use it?"
  "Ah oh! Are there any traps I'm missing?"
  "I'm not seeing any big yellow threats. Can you see any?"
  "Ok, I could block yellow with column 5, row 3"
  "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now otherwise yellow will win right?"
  "Would row 6 not be a threat in the future?"
  "I only have one move left and don't see anything obvious."
  "Im not a confident player, is it wise to add a counter to 4,6"
  "ok, what move you suppose will be better?"
  "what would you suggest"
  "Which move would be the best one and why"

Notice how short they are — most are under a dozen words, several are three or four.
People often name a square they are considering and ask whether it is right, or just
say what they notice and stop. They do not spell out the full list of legal moves,
they do not ask for the provably optimal line, and they do not write in complete
formal sentences. Typos and half-sentences are fine.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

We need to play the Othello endgame puzzle. We are Black (B). Need to choose move from legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. We need to maximize final disc count assuming optimal opponent play. We have view_board and consult_assistant. We are playing as a parent, 43, some college, weekly AI usage. Should ask assistant maybe to help, but we have limited budget and time. Must use natural short messages.

We need to reason ourselves too. Let's analyze board.

Row1: a1 . b1 W c1 W d1 W e1 W f1 W g1 W h1 .
Row2: a2 W b2 B c2 W d2 W e2 B f2 W g2 . h2 B
Row3: a3 . b3 B c3 B d3 W e3 W f3 W g3 W h3 B
Row4: a4 B b4 B c4 W d4 B e4 W f4 W g4 W h4 B
Row5: a5 B b5 B c5 W d5 W e5 B f5 W g5 W h5 B
Row6: a6 W b6 . c6 B d6 W e6 W f6 B g6 W h6 B
Row7: a7 . b7 . c7 W d7 W e7 W f7 W g7 W h7 B
Row8: a8 . b8 . c8 . d8 W e8 B f8 W g8 W h8 B

Empty: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,a8,b8,c8.

Legal moves for Black: g2,b6,a7,b7,b8,c8. Need to evaluate.

Let's see each move:

Move g2: Place at g2. Adjacent lines: to left along row2: g2-f2(W)-e2(B) => flips f2? Wait direction left: from g2 to f2 is W, then e2 is B, so yes flips f2. Up-left? g2-f1(W)-e? e1 is W not B. Up? g2-g1(W)-? h? no. Down-left? g2-f3(W)-e4? e4 is W not B. Down? g2-g3(W)-... but no B in that direction? g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W then edge, no B. Down-right? h3 is B? h3 is B adjacent, but direction down-right from g2 to h3 is one step, but need line of opponent discs between g2 and B on other side. For direction down-right, from g2 to h3 is immediate neighbor B, no opponent discs in between, so no flip. Up-right? h1 is . empty. Left-down? f3(W) then e4(W) then d5(W) then c6(B). So along diagonal down-left? Actually from g2 to f3 is down-left (SW). f3 W, e4 W, d5 W, c6 B. That would flip f3,e4,d5. Nice. Also maybe other directions: up-left f1(W), e? e1 is W not B. Down g3(W), g4(W), g5(W), g6(W), g7(W), g8(W) no B. Right h2 is B adjacent, no opponent. So g2 flips f2, f3, e4, d5? Wait d5 is W and c6 is B, so yes d5 flips. And maybe more? Let's map: direction SW: squares f3(W), e4(W), d5(W), c6(B). So flips f3,e4,d5. Also left: f2(W), e2(B) flips f2. So total flips: f2, f3, e4, d5. Also maybe direction down-right? from g2 to h3 is B immediate, no. Down-left we accounted. Up-left? f1(W), e? e1 is W. No B beyond. Up? g1(W). So 4 discs flipped. After move, Black gets g2 and flips those 4 to B. So net +5 discs (gain 4 flips + placed disc). Let's check if any other flips: direction left along row2 f2(W) e2(B) yes. Direction down-left f3(W) e4(W) d5(W) c6(B) yes. Any other lines? Up-left from g2: f1(W), e? e isn't on same diagonal? Actually up-left from g2 is f1 (row1 col f). Then next would be e0 (offboard). So only f1, which is W but no B beyond. No flip. Down-right: h3(B) immediate, no W between. Up-right: h1(.). So only those two lines. Good.

Move b6: Place at b6. Let's examine. Adjacent: left a6 is W, then no beyond? a6 W, beyond is offboard, so no. Right c6 is B immediate, no. Up a5? up-left? Actually directions from b6:
- Up (north): b5 B immediate? b5 is B, so no W between.
- Down (south): b7 . empty.
- Left (west): a6 W, then offboard. No B beyond.
- Right (east): c6 B immediate.
- Up-left (NW): a5 B immediate? a5 is B at col a row5? Wait a5 is B, diagonal from b6 to a5 is NW. That's B immediate, no W between.
- Up-right (NE): c5 W, d4 B. So flips c5. Because c5 W, then d4 B. Yes.
- Down-left (SW): a7 . empty.
- Down-right (SE): c7 W, d8 W, e? e9 offboard; no B beyond? Actually c7 W, d8 W, e9 offboard, so no. Wait could there be B further? d8 is W, e8 is B but e8 is not on same diagonal (SE from c7 goes to d8 then e9). Actually from b6 SE direction: c7 (row7 col c) is W, d8 (row8 col d) is W, e9 offboard, no B beyond. So no flip.
- Up? Also check up two? Already checked. What about direction up (north) along column b: b5 B immediate, no. Direction down: b7 . empty. Up-right NE we did. Down-right SE no. 
But also maybe direction west (left) along row6: a6 W, then beyond is offboard. No. 
What about direction up-left from b6? a5 is B immediate. 
Direction up-right is only line with W then B. Also maybe direction to the left and up? Already done.

Any other diagonal? b6 to a7 is SW, a7 empty. b6 to c5 is NE (c5 W, d4 B). Yes.

So b6 flips only c5. Net gain +2? Actually placed disc +1 and flip one, so +2 total? Wait Black gets b6, and flips c5 from W->B. So Black gains 2 discs, White loses 1. Net difference +2? Actually Black disc count increases by 2 (new disc + flipped), White decreases by 1. In terms of total disc count at end, yes.

But maybe there are other flips? Let's double-check board coordinates carefully. b6 is row6 col b. Up direction: row5 col b = b5 = B. So no. Up-left: a5 = B immediate. Up-right: c5 = W. d4 = B. So c5 flips. Down: b7 empty. Down-right: c7 = W. d8 = W. e9 offboard. No B beyond. Down-left: a7 empty. Left: a6 = W. Offboard beyond. Right: c6 = B immediate. So only c5 flips. Good.

Move a7: Place at a7. Check lines from a7. Directions:
- Right (east): b7 empty. c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. So from a7 to the right, b7 is empty, so not contiguous opponent discs from a7 because immediate right is empty. Actually line must be continuous opponent discs starting adjacent. Since b7 is empty, no flip horizontally.
- Down (south): a8 empty.
- Up-right (NE): b8 empty. c? offboard? Wait NE from a7 goes to b8. b8 is empty, so no.
- Down-right (SE): b8 empty. So no.
- Right-down? Actually we need all directions: East, SE, South, SW (offboard), W (offboard), NW (offboard), N (a6 is W?), let's see North: a6 W, then a5 B. So up (north) from a7: a6 W, a5 B. That flips a6. Good.
- Northeast: b6 . empty. So no.
- East: b7 . empty. No.
- Southeast: b8 . empty. No.
- South: a8 . empty. No.
But also from a7, direction up-right? Wait up-right from a7 is b6? Actually coordinates: row decreases when going up. So from a7 (col a row7), up is a6 (row6), up-right is b6 (row6 col b). b6 is empty currently (but note b6 is a legal move, but currently empty). So no. Up-right further would be c5 etc but need contiguous. Since b6 empty, no flip in that diagonal.

Down-right from a7 is b8 empty. So no.

Thus a7 only flips a6. Also maybe direction down? a8 empty. So only a6 flips. Net gain +2.

Wait also from a7 direction east: b7 empty, so no. Direction east second step c7 is W but not adjacent (b7 empty breaks). So no. What about direction up then? a6 W, a5 B. So flips a6. Any other? Let's check diagonal down-left from a7 impossible. So a7 gives one flip.

Move b7: Place at b7. Directions: 
- Up: b6 empty. So no vertical.
- Down: b8 empty.
- Left: a7 empty.
- Right: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. So flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. That's 5 flips! Good.
- Up-left: a6 W, then offboard? Wait from b7 up-left is a6? Let's compute: row up (6), col left (a). a6 is W. Beyond a6 offboard. So no B beyond. No flip.
- Up-right: c6 B immediate? c6 is B at row6 col c. So no W between. No flip.
- Down-left: a8 empty.
- Down-right: c8 empty.
- Up: b6 empty.
- Down: b8 empty.
Thus b7 flips c7-g7 (5 discs). Plus b7 = gain of 6? Actually new disc + flips = +6 for Black, White loses 5. So net shift +6.

But wait check: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. Yes continuous. So b7 is very strong.

Move b8: Place at b8. Directions:
- Up: b7 empty. So no.
- Right: c8 empty. d? Actually c8 is empty legal move. So no.
- Down: offboard.
- Left: a8 empty.
- Up-right: c7 W, d6 W, e5 B. So flips c7,d6? Wait carefully: from b8 up-right is c7 (row7 col c) = W. Then d6 (row6 col d) = W. Then e5 (row5 col e) = B. Yes. So flips c7 and d6. Check if any beyond? That's it. So two flips there.
- Up-left: a7 empty.
- Right-up? Already did up-right. Right (east): c8 empty. So no.
- Down-right: offboard (row9). 
- Down? offboard.
What about direction up (north): b7 empty. No.
Direction right (east): c8 empty. No.
Direction left? a8 empty.
Any other diagonal? From b8 down-left? offboard. So only up-right yields flips. Also maybe direction west? no. Also direction south? offboard. So b8 flips c7 and d6. Net gain +3? Wait placed disc flips 2 => +3 total discs.

Wait check also direction east? c8 empty. No. Direction north-east? yes. Direction north? b7 empty. Direction north-west? a7 empty. So b8 gives +3.

Move c8: Place at c8. Directions:
- Up: c7 W, c6 B. So flips c7. Good.
- Left: b8 empty. No.
- Right: d8 W, e8 B. So flips d8. Good.
- Up-left: b7 empty. No.
- Up-right: d7 W, e6 W, f5 W, g4 W, h3 B. So from c8 up-right: d7 W, e6 W, f5 W, g4 W, h3 B. Flips d7,e6,f5,g4. That's 4 flips! Check squares: d7 is W, e6 is W, f5 is W, g4 is W, h3 is B. Yes all continuous. So flips d7,e6,f5,g4. 
- Down? offboard.
- Down-left? offboard.
- Down-right? offboard.
- Left-up? already up-left.
- Left? b8 empty.
Any other? Up direction we have c7 W then c6 B, so flips c7. Right direction d8 W then e8 B => flips d8.

Total flips for c8: c7,d8,d7,e6,f5,g4. That's 6 flips! Plus new disc = +7 disc difference. Black gets 7 new discs, White loses 6. That's a huge swing. Check if c8 is legal? Yes c8 is listed in legal moves. Let's double-check lines for c8:
- North: c7 W, c6 B. Yes.
- Northwest: b7 . empty. No.
- West: b8 . empty. No.
- Southwest: offboard? Actually from c8 down-left is b9 offboard.
- South: offboard.
- Southeast: offboard.
- East: d8 W, e8 B. Yes.
- Northeast: d7 W, e6 W, f5 W, g4 W, h3 B. Yes. Continuous W's? d7=W, e6=W, f5=W, g4=W, h3=B. All good.
- Also maybe direction north-east? Already accounted. What about direction north-west? b7 is empty. So no.
What about direction west? b8 empty. No.
Thus c8 is amazing. Let's verify counts. Black currently has 20. White 34. Empty 10.

If we play c8, Black flips 6 discs to Black. So Black gets 20 + 7 = 27 immediately. White loses 6 => 34 - 6 = 28. After this move, Black 27, White 28. Then there are 9 empties left: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,b8,a8? Wait c8 now filled. Let's list empties after c8: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,b8,a8. Actually check if any other empties become filled? No. So 9 empties. But the puzzle says play to end; we need to choose the move that yields max final count assuming optimal opponent.

c8 seems very strong. However we must consider that after c8, the board state changes and opponent may have some responses that flip many back.

Let's analyze deeper. Since we need to solve puzzle to end, maybe we should ask assistant for help evaluating c8 vs b7 vs other. But we can also try to compute ourselves. Since this is endgame with 10 empty squares, maybe we can do exhaustive reasoning. But time is limited. We can also ask assistant: "c8 looks big, is it the best?" or "Which move gives me the most discs at the end?"

Given persona: parent, some college, weekly AI usage. Short messages. Might ask assistant something like "c8 flips a bunch but will white just flip them back? what move is best?" or "I'm leaning c8 or b7, which is better?" The assistant can reply with evaluation.

We have limited question budget, but we can ask a few. We should not waste too much time; need to finish the puzzle. We can perhaps ask one question to confirm, then play.

But before asking, let's see if we can reason if c8 is indeed optimal. Let's compute lines.

After c8: board becomes:
Row1: a1 . b1 W c1 W d1 W e1 W f1 W g1 W h1 .
Row2: a2 W b2 B c2 W d2 W e2 B f2 W g2 . h2 B
Row3: a3 . b3 B c3 B d3 W e3 W f3 W g3 W h3 B
Row4: a4 B b4 B c4 W d4 B e4 W f4 W g4 B h4 B  (g4 flipped to B)
Row5: a5 B b5 B c5 W d5 W e5 B f5 B g5 W h5 B (f5 flipped)
Row6: a6 W b6 . c6 B d6 W e6 W f6 B g6 W h6 B (d6 remains W? Wait d6 was W, check flip: c8 NE flips d7,e6,f5,g4. It does NOT flip d6. d6 remains W.)
Wait e6 is flipped to B. So row6: a6 W, b6 ., c6 B, d6 W, e6 B, f6 B, g6 W, h6 B.
Row7: a7 . b7 . c7 B d7 B e7 W f7 W g7 W h7 B (c7 and d7 flipped)
Row8: a8 . b8 . c8 B d8 B e8 B f8 W g8 W h8 B (d8 flipped)

Let's update White discs after c8: original white 34 minus flipped {c7,d8,d7,e6,f5,g4} = 6, so 28 White. Black: 20 + 1 (c8) +6 = 27.

Now White's turn. Need to find White legal moves. White empties: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,b8,a8? Wait a8 still empty; b8 empty; a7 empty; b7 empty; b6 empty; a3 empty; g2 empty; a1,h1 empty. Also maybe c8 is filled, so empties: a1,a3,a7,a8,b6,b7,b8,g2,h1. That's 9 squares.

White can move on any of these that trap at least one Black disc between new W and another W.

Let's check each empty for White:

a1: Adjacent. Right: b1 W immediate? b1 is W, but need opponent discs between new W and another W. Since b1 is W adjacent, there are no opponent discs between a1 and b1. So no horizontal. Down: a2 W immediate? a2 is W. No. Down-right: b2 B, c3 B? Wait diagonal from a1 down-right: b2 is B, c3 is B, d4 is B, e5 is B, f6 is B, g7 is W! That's a line: b2 B, c3 B, d4 B, e5 B, f6 B, g7 W. Are they all B? Let's check: b2 B, c3 B, d4 B, e5 B, f6 B, g7 W. Yes! So a1 would flip b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. So a1 is a legal White move, flipping 5 Black discs. Huge.

h1: Adjacent. Left: g1 W immediate, no opponent between. Down: h2 B, h3 B, h4 B, h5 B, h6 B, h7 B, h8 B? Wait h2 B, h3 B, h4 B, h5 B, h6 B, h7 B, h8 B. No W beyond? Actually down from h1 goes to h2 (row2). All squares h2 to h8 are B, but then row9 offboard, no W beyond. So no flip down. Down-left: g2 empty. Left-down? Other directions: down-left from h1: g2 empty. So no. So h1 might not be legal? Let's check other directions: left along row1: g1 W immediate. Up? offboard. So h1 is not legal unless some other diagonal. Up-left? g0 offboard. So no.

g2: empty. For White at g2. Adjacent: left f2 W immediate? f2 is W. But need B between. No. Right h2 B immediate? No W beyond? Actually g2 right: h2 B, beyond h1 . empty. No. Up: g1 W immediate. No. Down: g3 W immediate? g3 is W. Wait board row3 col g is W. So down from g2 to g3 is W immediate, no B between. Down-left: f3 W immediate. No. Down-right: h3 B immediate. No W beyond? h3 is B, beyond offboard (i4). So no. Up-left: f1 W immediate. Up-right: h1 . empty. Left: f2 W. So g2 may not be legal for White. Let's check direction down from g2: g3 is W, immediate, so no flip. Up-left? f1 is W immediate. So no. What about direction up-right h1 . empty. So no.

a3: empty. For White at a3. Right: b3 B, c3 B, d3 W. So flips b3,c3. Down: a4 B, a5 B, a6 W. So flips a4,a5. Up-right: b2 B, c1 W. Flips b2. Right-down? b4 B, c5 W. Flips b4. Down-right: b4 B already? Wait diagonal SE from a3: b4 B, c5 W. Flips b4. Also maybe direction down two? a4 B, a5 B, a6 W flips a4,a5. So a3 is legal and flips several: b3,c3, a4,a5, b2, b4. Let's count: b3 (B), c3 (B) via East. b2 (B) via NE. b4 (B) via SE? Actually SE from a3: b4 B, c5 W => flips b4. Also South: a4 B, a5 B, a6 W => flips a4,a5. So total flips: b3,c3,b2,b4,a4,a5 = 6 flips. That's huge for White. So if Black plays c8, White can respond a3 and flip many.

b6: empty. For White at b6. Need to check. Up-left from b6: a5 B, offboard? Actually a5 B immediate? Wait b6 up-left is a5. a5 is B. No W beyond? Offboard. No flip. Up: b5 B immediate. No flip. Up-right: c5 W immediate (since c5 is W), but need opponent discs between new W and other W. So not. Right: c6 B immediate; beyond c7 B now? Wait after c8, c7 is B (flipped). So from b6 to c6 is B, not W. No. Down-right: c7 B? c7 is B. No W between. Down: b7 empty. Down-left: a7 empty. Left: a6 W immediate; no B between. Right? c6 B; d? d6 W but not contiguous because c6 is B, not opponent. So b6 is not legal? Let's check diagonal up-right: c5 W immediate, no B between. So no. What about direction right-up? same. So b6 seems no legal line for White.

a7: empty. For White at a7. Down: a8 empty. Right: b7 empty. Up: a6 W immediate? Wait a6 is W. So no flip up. Up-right: b6 empty. Down-right: b8 empty. So a7 maybe not legal? Check direction right? b7 empty. Up-right: b6 empty. There is no line of opponent. So a7 illegal.

b7: empty. For White at b7. For White to move at b7, need traps. Right: c7 B (now B after c8), d7 B, e7 W? Wait e7 is W. Actually row7 after c8: c7 B, d7 B, e7 W. So from b7 to c7 is B, d7 is B, e7 is W. That would be B,B,W. But there must be contiguous opponent discs (Black) between new White disc and another White disc. So the line is c7 B, d7 B, e7 W. Yes, since c7 and d7 are opponent (Black) and e7 is own color (White)! Wait is e7 W? Yes, board row7 col e is W originally. It hasn't changed. So b7 would flip c7 and d7. Also maybe other directions: down: b8 empty. Up: b6 empty. Left: a7 empty. Up-left: a6 W immediate. Up-right: c6 B immediate? c6 is B. No W beyond? Actually c6 B, beyond d5 W but not contiguous because c6 is not opponent of White? Wait White opponent is Black. c6 is Black. To flip, we need a line of Black discs ending with a White disc. **Endgame lesson:** don’t just ask “how many do I flip now?” Ask:

1. **Does my move give White a corner or stable edge/file?**  
   Once White got the **a-file**, many of those discs became hard/impossible to win back.

3. **Count final discs, not immediate flips.**  
   In this game Black ended **24–40**, so White’s edge/file control mattered far more than a short-term flip.

So: **don’t blindly avoid all edges**—edges can be good. But in endgames, avoid giving your opponent an edge/file that becomes stable, especially connected to a corner.
